overview: Denicker reveals the real names behind nicked players by decoding the S38PacketPlayerListItem ADD_PLAYER entries: it takes the base64 'textures' property from the joined player's GameProfile, base64-decodes it, parses the JSON with Gson, and reads the profileName field embedded in the signed skin payload. When that real name differs from the displayed (nicked) name, the pair is queued as real=nick. When an S02PacketChat message containing 'has joined' arrives, a background thread matches the nick against the queue and raises a notification, and with Overlay Support enabled re-logs the chat line through the client logger with the real name substituted. The module is purely receive-side: it sends no packets.

sections.p: onPacketReceive intercepts S38PacketPlayerListItem with Action.ADD_PLAYER and inspects the first AddPlayerData entry (get(0)). It pulls the GameProfile, reads the 'textures' Property, base64-decodes its value into a JSON document, and extracts profileName. The Mojang-signed skin payload carries the account's real profile name as plaintext metadata, and Hypixel-style nick systems keep that payload intact while changing only the display name - so profileName != nickedName is the denick signal. Self-joins are skipped by comparing against the local player's name, and already-queued nicks are deduped. The whole decode is wrapped in a try/catch that prints the stack trace on failure, so malformed payloads are skipped silently-ish.

When an S02PacketChat message contains 'has joined', the module spawns a new Thread that iterates the denickQueue: for each real=nick pair, if the join message contains the nick, it registers a notification ('real is nicked as nick') and, with Overlay Support enabled, writes a re-logged line to the client logger with control codes stripped and the nick replaced by the real name. Each 'has joined' message gets its own thread, so a lobby burst spawns one thread per message, each scanning the whole queue.

denickQueue is cleared on every WorldChangedEvent, so the denick data never survives a server or world switch. The module reads only the first player entry per S38 packet and only the 'textures' property, so it depends entirely on the server forwarding the signed skin payload with its profileName intact - servers that strip or randomize that field (or that do not send textures in ADD_PLAYER) produce no denicks. The overlay path is a logger.info call, not a chat packet, so the substituted line is visible only to the local client and its log.

files.label: Denicker.java
files.explanation: The module is receive-side only. onPacketReceive handles S38PacketPlayerListItem ADD_PLAYER entries - base64-decoding the textures property, parsing profileName out of the skin JSON with Gson, and queueing real=nick pairs - and S02PacketChat messages containing 'has joined', which trigger a per-message Thread that matches the queue and raises notifications or re-logs the line with the real name. onWorldChanged clears the queue. No packet is ever sent.

countering.label: Text (chat frequency and repeat similarity)
countering.explanation: Denicker itself sends nothing - it only decodes S38 skin payloads and reads S02 chat - so no packet check can fire on the denick action directly; the enforcement surface is the chat abuse denicking feeds. NCP's Text check scores every chat message into frequency buckets and penalizes repeats and post-join chatter over an 8-second window, which is exactly the profile of the scripted /msg harassment that follows a denick (AutoGroomer-style targeting). The honest boundary: Text counters the automation that uses the denicked names, not the extraction itself - a Denicker sitting idle in a lobby produces no chat traffic for Text to see.

countering.label: Commands (targeted /msg rate)
countering.explanation: The practical use of a denick is targeted messaging, and every such message is a /msg command, so NCP's Commands check - which scores commands per second in data.commandsShortTermWeight and flags bursts over cc.commandsShortTermLevel - is the check that constrains the post-denick flow. Spamming the freshly-identified name produces the same short-term command burst the check was built for. As with Text, the boundary is explicit: Commands cannot see Denicker's receive-side parsing; it only caps the command traffic that gives denicked names their value.

countering.label: Captcha (auto-armed chat gate)
countering.explanation: NCP's Captcha check arms a chat gate once suspicion accumulates: chat is blocked until the player answers a server-generated question, and wrong answers repeat the question and raise the violation. For the automation that follows a denick, the gate is decisive - a scripted /msg flow cannot answer the captcha, so the moment any chat check arms the gate, the targeted-harassment pipeline stalls. Denicker's own receive-side parsing is untouched by the gate; the check counters the automated chat that denicking enables rather than the name extraction itself.
